entry.code_revision: THE AUTHOR'S OWN MODEL AND DECISION LIBRARY, with a first-party loopback System One wire shim: plantwaterer/allec at e54027aa1f865bdd25724e9b3c1acb51b2bbc3c3. Library-only submission, with no author HTTP server. The shim calls the author's unchanged README entry point LenAvgBayesEngine(model=local_model, device=cuda) from lenavg_bayes_engine; it does not substitute the older single-pass DikitEngine. Full Gemma-4-31B-derived weights and trained decision head are measured together. Native defaults remain BF16 backbone, CPU FP64 L01-post head, bidirectional global jev_mem attention and causal sliding layers, max_len 32,768, tokens_per_batch 32,768, l_star 939 and averaging enabled. Short-request routing uses structural characters, not token counts. Native four-order choice averaging for menus of at most 52 options, two-order noul averaging, deterministic author temperatures and Bayesian head correction are retained. Menus above 52 retain native chunk scoring, model-selected finalists and the final round, including total 0.001 probability mass on discarded final options. Requests are serialized because native forward hooks and averaging flags are mutable. Native probabilities are transported unchanged; no generated text, host retry, answer repair, stock causal generation, quantization or stock-vLLM equivalence. Score criteria are unsupported: the shim returns native-domain HTTP 422 before the author's length helper can hit .items() on score-list criteria, without score-to-choice conversion. Native context/state-shown refusals also return HTTP 422. No truncation, raised context cap, split state or fallback inference. The native renderer's crop followed by check_state_shown is transcribed as a refusal before forwarding. The first-party observer additionally refuses any alternative forward missing the full normalized state or exceeding 32,768 tokens; this is a disclosed no-truncation transport adaptation. Structured state uses native JSON conversion, preserving native structural-length routing on the original state. USAGE IS FIRST-PARTY OBSERVED ACCOUNTING: numeric input_tokens sums the tokenizer lengths of every actually forwarded prompt, including averaged option orders, packed sequences and second rounds; it is expanded prefill, not a single read and not an author-native billing contract. Output_tokens is 0 because no continuation is generated. The frozen TypeSafe adapter and measurement driver remain unchanged, including the 120 s transport timeout. Decision Index base.py is pinned at 9eb2dbe2a358004c8782c66e40a83ac07b953fec; no Decision Index suite or training code runs. Runtime receipts retain source, package RECORD and tokenizer hashes; torch 2.14.1, CUDA 13.0, transformers 5.12.1, tokenizers 0.22.2, numpy 2.2.6, safetensors 0.8.0 and accelerate 1.15.0. Source review found no benchmark-item answer lookup in the serving closure; framework internals were not exhaustively audited. Author code and weights ran only on the disposable rented pod, with verified local artifacts, read-only mounts, empty credentials, offline flags and network cut before sealed input.

This is a PEFT adapter plus base model, not a standalone full fine-tuned checkpoint. The author supplies a single-question demo with ten implemented labels and describes a larger label table. The shim preserves its Context/Question/Options/Answer prompt, native state serialization, original option order, last-token hidden state, candidate lm_head projection, float logits and candidate-restricted softmax. No chat template, prompt sanitization, truncation or generated text. It loads explicit Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration plus PEFT, then get_base_model().model.language_model and lm_head, with BF16 CUDA base and ordinary PEFT adapter dtype behavior. Stock efficient SDPA is selected by the locked runtime; no attention override, quantization, CPU fallback, host retry or answer repair. Under the 31 Oct preregistration amendment, this 27B row ran the cache-free single-prefill path: use_cache=False for each independent complete prefill and empty_cache() before each score call after prior tensors leave scope; no past state is reused. Multiple questions use separate serial passes; no invented multi-slot packing. DECLARED EXTENSIONS: noul maps proposition/negation in true/false order, with instructions and literal Not (instructions) as absent-description fallback; score preserves ordered levels and returns the complete distribution keyed by zero-based index strings. The card's 255-label single-token constraint is interpreted by A-Z followed by the first 229 lexically ordered uppercase pairs that tokenize singly, ending at JT; split-token pairs are skipped. This is a disclosed interpretation, not proof of an unavailable complete author training table. Public pod parity verified exact token IDs and bit-identical probabilities between the original cached author readout and the cache-free shim on all nine short public type/width cases. Long public probes verify rendering, token IDs, wire shapes and usage; no long-length cached probability comparison is claimed. 8,192 is training length, not a refusal cap; the demo forwards every unpadded token without a native total-length check. Architectural 262,144 positions do not establish empirical capacity. No context cap is added; genuine unsupported type/candidate contracts may return HTTP 422, while framework/OOM faults remain HTTP 500. First-party HTTP input usage sums every actually forwarded prompt, including repeated state across question passes; output_tokens is 0. The author supplies no HTTP server or usage billing contract. The frozen TypeSafe adapter and driver retain the 120 s transport timeout. Locked runtime: torch 2.11.0, CUDA 13.0, transformers 5.19.0, tokenizers 0.23.3, PEFT 0.21.2, safetensors 0.8.0; source/runtime/tokenizer hashes retained. Source review found no benchmark-item lookup in the selected author readout; upstream framework internals were not exhaustively audited. Numerical and author-code execution occurred only on the disposable rented pod, with verified local base/adapter, read-only mounts, empty credentials, offline flags and network cut.

entry.code_revision: THE AUTHOR'S OWN NATIVE COMPILER AND LAYOUT, measured at agentscope-ai/Piccolo-27B@9cab0ecef7372d29ac83b50ac5e49cead2caa173: piccolo_inference.py sha256 9d7253bba12525788481386da0475811db5c83e33c979551b2bc5805015b7415, piccolo_layout.py sha256 2dda6a8fd9140a5ae573950a04578de2241b8bf533247cda734b45bdeca7911f. No author HTTP server exists. Our first-party resident HTTP/usage shim loads the complete pinned safetensors checkpoint, including indexed auxiliary/MTP files, and invokes the pinned FlexCompiler and layout; the GGUF siblings were not used. The whole request is compiled before any forward. Native flex_twice defaults are preserved: max_context 65,536, row ceiling 65,535, request-wide single-read input <=3,000 tokens repeats the user input within each row when all repeated rows fit. Repetition concatenates tokens within one forward, not two independent forwards. One complete decoder call per question, use_cache=False, no chunking, truncation, prompt splitting or raised ceiling. Full-attention pre-hooks replace attention masks with dense BF16 zeros; linear layers remain unchanged. Candidate output-embedding rows are multiplied by the final hidden state in FP32, softmax temperature 1. Native choice, boolean noul and ordered score mappings are preserved; score keys are numeric strings. Input usage sums actual input_ids lengths across all question forwards, including both copies; output usage is zero, with no text generation. An over-ceiling row returns HTTP 422 and usage 0/0 for the whole request before inference. The first-party tokenizer-only counter is a separate transcription; pod-side public parity compared complete token IDs, candidates, keys, metadata and repetition behavior against the native compiler. No author code was executed on the workshop servers. The frozen TypeSafe adapter and serial driver retain the 120 s transport timeout; no host retry, answer repair, ensemble or stock-base substitution. Container base python:3.12.12-bookworm@sha256:6760942332f453ec141ea470fa3bfb790e84e11edcf0b6331b98bee6091a7b69, hash-locked upstream wheels: torch 2.14.1, CUDA 13.0, transformers 5.12.1, tokenizers 0.22.2, accelerate 1.15.0, safetensors 0.8.0. FLA, fla-core, causal-conv1d and kernels distributions are absent; Qwen3.5 linear attention and convolution use the native Torch fallback. Runtime, author-source and tokenizer hashes were retained. Source review found no benchmark-item lookup or item-specific routing; the fixed JEVLAB sentinel is a chat-template split marker. No author main() or diagnostic output mode is invoked. Author imports and numerical execution occurred only on the isolated disposable rented pod, with local hash-verified weights, read-only mounts, empty credentials, offline flags and network cut.
